Issued at 305 PM CDT Thu Oct 15 2026

Through Friday night:

An expansive fall storm system centered over the mid- 
Mississippi Valley is lifting a warm front into Illinois and 
Indiana this afternoon. Deep atmospheric moisture is being drawn
northward ahead of this system, yielding precipitable water 
(PWAT) values up to 1.75-2.0 inches (near record highs) for 
this time of year. This moisture will support narrow corridors 
of torrential rain late this afternoon and evening, particularly
where convective elements train east-northeastward. While not 
everyone will experience torrential downpours, scattered to 
numerous rain showers are expected area-wide through early this 
evening. The threat for isolated thunderstorms remains low, but 
with the primary MUCAPE reservoir lifting across east-central 
Illinois into northern Indiana by early evening, any 
thunderstorm activity should remain primarily south of I-80. A 
strong storm or two cannot be ruled out through early evening, 
but that threat will be confined even farther south (generally 
south of a line from Gibson City, IL to Remington, IN), aligning
well with the SPC Day 1 outlook. 

The primary low-pressure system will track directly over 
northern Illinois early this evening, then deepen as it shifts 
northeast into lower Michigan tonight. Expect a brief period of 
lower ceilings and reduced visibility for a few hours as the low
moves overhead. Conditions will improve rapidly later tonight 
following a sharp cold front. In its wake, northwest winds will 
become gusty (3035 mph) overnight, while strong cold air 
advection drops temperatures into the 40s to low 50s by early 
Friday morning. Breezy conditions (gusts of 35 to 40 mph) will 
persist through Friday due to strong pressure rises behind the 
departing low and ahead of a 1035+ mb surface high building in 
from the Plains. Even stronger northerly winds (~45 mph) are 
projected over southern Lake Michigan Friday afternoon and 
evening. Onshore flow will push some of these higher winds 
inland across far northern Porter County, Indiana, where a Wind 
Advisory is in effect from 1:00 PM to 10:00 PM CDT Friday.

Much cooler weather is expected Friday, with temperatures 
hovering in the low to mid-50s as the coldest airmass of the 
season arrives under a sharp trough moving across the western 
Great Lakes. Steepening low- to mid-level lapse rates will 
support a diurnal increase in scattered showers, especially 
Friday afternoon. While showers will remain hit-or-miss across 
interior northern Illinois, favorable lake-effect conditions 
will bring widespread showers and potentially isolated 
thunderstorms to southern Lake Michigan and adjacent shorelines 
Friday afternoon and evening, supported by lake-induced 
equilibrium heights exceeding 20,000 feet.

KJB

Friday night into Saturday:

The progressive pattern continues as the surface low departs 
and surface high pressure moves toward the middle Mississippi 
River Valley. Lingering lake-effect clouds and persistent cold 
air advection will keep winds slower to diminish Friday night 
across eastern Illinois and northwest Indiana. Farther west, 
clearing skies and light winds near the approaching surface 
ridge axis across northwest Illinois will set the stage for a 
potential freeze. In collaboration with WFOs MKX and DVN, a 
Freeze Watch was issued for Boone, Winnebago, and Ogle counties,
where lows near 30F are expected early Saturday morning. 
Widespread frost is also likely to extend farther east and 
south, where Frost Advisories may eventually be needed, 
potentially reaching as far east as some of the western Chicago 
suburbs. 

Saturday will bring full sunshine and weak winds as 
high pressure moves directly overhead, though the chilly start 
will cap afternoon highs in the 50s. Saturday night will be 
chilly again, with the coldest temperatures favored east of I-55
beneath the lightest winds near the high's center, likely 
requiring additional frost headlines.

Southwesterly return flow will establish by Sunday on the 
backside of the departing high, initiating a warming trend into 
early next week.

KJB/Borchardt
